scope: the ERP identity the deployed executor runs as
what_this_proves: The credential the deployed ingress and review services hold is a purpose-made ERP user whose rights were read back off the live site during this run: it performs every supplier operation the system needs, and it cannot delete a record, widen its own role, or reach a financial document.
not_proven_here: That the deployed services are USING this credential. That is a Secret Manager version plus a Cloud Run revision, checked by scripts/doctor.sh and re-proven end to end by spikes/core_contracts/harness.py.
Anything about the owner credential's own scope. It is a full System Manager by design, lives only in .env.secrets, and is used only by scripts/erp.py.

criteria.requirement: The credential deployed services hold belongs to a user carrying one custom role, not to the site owner

checks.detail: executor identity is not the site owner (redacted)

criteria.note: Read back from the live site, so re-granting the owner's key to the deployed services fails this rather than passing quietly.

criteria.requirement: Role 'Keplaria Executor' grants exactly the rights app/executor/frappe.py exercises, on exactly the doctypes it touches

checks.detail: no permission rows outside the contract

criteria.note: Compared over every flag Frappe stores, so a right introduced by a future version is a failure by default rather than an unnoticed grant.

criteria.requirement: Every ERP operation the deployed system performs succeeds under the scoped identity

checks.detail: create_supplier_if_absent: {"external_id": "TEST Scoped Executor Probe SAS", "created": true}
set_supplier_hold: {"external_id": "TEST Scoped Executor Probe SAS", "created": true}
clear_supplier_hold: {"external_id": "TEST Scoped Executor Probe SAS", "created": true}

criteria.note: Enumerated from app/executor/frappe.py's public operations. A new operation needing a right the role lacks fails here, at the cost of one line, rather than in a deployed run.

criteria.requirement: The executor cannot delete any record it can create

checks.detail: DELETE Supplier/TEST Scoped Executor Probe SAS -> HTTP 403 (record readable: HTTP 200)

criteria.note: Each attempt targets a record this run created and confirms it is readable first, so a 403 is a permission refusal rather than Frappe not finding the record.

criteria.requirement: The executor cannot create roles, permissions or users
criteria.note: The Custom DocPerm attempt is the one that matters: it is the exact write that would widen this role, and it is the write every other criterion here depends on being refused.

criteria.requirement: The executor cannot read or write invoices, payments, ledgers or company records
Frappe's own System User baseline is measured and stated, not implied away by the word 'scoped'

baseline doctypes the executor can also CREATE: ['Contact']; probe records removed: ['Contact/1k1hah3b46']
